name: Telegraph cryptic crossword, All New book 4 No 8

book.title: The Telegraph All New Cryptic Crosswords 4

clue.text: Savoury pie with crinkly chips on trays

indicators.note: crinkly chips are wavy and twisted, so the letters that follow are bent out of their order

blocks.note: all twelve letters of these three words are used

explanation.surface: A café order: a pie served alongside crinkle-cut chips on trays.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cornish pasty is a folded pastry case filled with meat and vegetables, a classic savoury pie from Cornwall.

clue.text: Go up into Lancs town for toilet water

indicators.note: in a down clue up means read from the bottom upwards, so the word runs backwards
into means placed inside, so the turned word goes within the town

blocks.note: taken as written
Colne is a mill town in Lancashire, northern England

explanation.surface: Visit a Lancashire town to buy perfume.
explanation.walkthrough: Lancs is the usual abbreviation for Lancashire, a county in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Eau de cologne is a light perfume, and toilet water is the English rendering of eau de toilette, the same kind of scent.

clue.text: Domestic cock and duck included in list

indicators.note: included in says one item is placed inside the other

blocks.note: a roster is a list of names, often a duty rota
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so the letter that looks like zero

explanation.surface: A farmyard cock and a duck are both included on a list of animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duck' sits beside cock as another farm bird, but it stands for nought.
explanation.definitionFit: A rooster is a male domestic chicken, which is what a cock is.

clue.text: Ones imprisoned by country, a republic

indicators.note: something imprisoned is held inside walls, so one word goes inside the other

blocks.note: India is a country
taken as written

explanation.surface: People locked up by a state described as a republic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country' looks like the definition, but it supplies the outer word; the answer is defined only as a republic.
explanation.definitionFit: Indonesia is a Southeast Asian state governed as a republic with an elected president.

blocks.note: first meaning: belonging to the comedian Bob Hope
second meaning: things one wishes for

explanation.walkthrough: The possessive of the comic Bob Hope's surname is spelled the same as the plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Hopes are wishes or ambitions for the future, so they are aspirations; Bob Hope was a famous American comedian.

clue.text: American ringing friend in NATO, perhaps

indicators.note: ringing means encircling, so the first word forms a ring around the second

blocks.note: Am is a standard abbreviation for American
a crony is a close friend

explanation.surface: An American telephoning a friend who works within the NATO alliance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ringing' suggests a phone call, but it means surrounding.
explanation.definitionFit: NATO is built from the initials of North Atlantic Treaty Organization, so it is an example of an acronym.

blocks.note: first meaning: as a verb, to cause or provoke
second meaning: as a verb, to set off or initiate

explanation.walkthrough: Prompt reads as an adjective meaning punctual, but both words are verbs here.
explanation.definitionFit: To trigger something is to set it off, which both prompts it and starts it.

blocks.note: a bairn is a Scottish and northern English word for a child
dad means father

explanation.surface: A child explains that his father draws cartoons.
explanation.walkthrough: Bruce Bairnsfather was a British cartoonist famous for his First World War character Old Bill.
explanation.definitionFit: Bruce Bairnsfather was a cartoonist, best known for wartime drawings of trench life.

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the phrase before it wraps around the number

blocks.note: the gangster Al Capone's first name
ordered, as in told someone to do something
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Al Capone is said to have ordered roughly fifty killings altogether.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ordered about' looks like bossing people around, but about belongs to the container: the gangster's name plus ordered wraps the Roman fifty.
explanation.definitionFit: All told is an idiom meaning counting everything together, the same as in total.

indicators.note: mostly means not all of it, so the final letter of the word is dropped
uncommonly suggests something done in an unusual way, so the letters are put in an unusual order

blocks.note: taken as written before it is cut short
W is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for a wide

explanation.surface: A river that, travelling upstream, opens out into an unusually wide range.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wide range' looks like one phrase, but wide is a separate piece: a wide is a ball bowled out of the batsman's reach in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: Purview is the scope or extent of something's authority or concern, i.e. its range.

clue.text: Piece of furniture lady's maid from Cardiff used?

blocks.note: first meaning: a sideboard with open shelves above for displaying plates, typical of Wales
second meaning: a servant who helps her mistress dress, coming from the Welsh capital

explanation.walkthrough: A dresser is both a kitchen cabinet and someone who helps another person get dressed; Cardiff is the capital of Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: The furniture is a traditional Welsh sideboard, and a lady's maid from Cardiff would be a dresser who is Welsh.

indicators.note: not tells us to leave something out of the word before it

blocks.note: Brighton is a seaside resort town on England's south coast
B is the standard abbreviation for British

explanation.surface: A fashionable seaside town described with a note that it is not in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Right on is slang for fashionably correct or up to date in attitude, so it is a synonym of trendy.

clue.text: Eagles shot round north of country

indicators.note: shot can mean ruined or wrecked, so the birds' letters are knocked into a new order
round means placed around, so the shuffled letters enclose the compass point

blocks.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: Eagles brought down by hunters in the northern part of some country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'North of country' reads like a region, but north is just the letter that goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Senegal is a country in West Africa, on the Atlantic coast.

blocks.note: first meaning: a castrated young male bovine
second meaning: as a verb, to guide or drive animals along

explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures one bullock among a herd, but herd is a verb here: to direct cattle where you want them to go.
explanation.definitionFit: A steer is a castrated bull raised for beef, and to steer is to guide or drive, as a drover does with cattle.

clue.text: Sailor harms ground, land by the sea subject to flooding

definitions.text: land by the sea subject to flooding

indicators.note: ground means crushed or milled, so the letters are broken up and remade

blocks.note: an old salt is an experienced sailor
taken as written, before being rearranged

explanation.surface: A sailor runs aground and does damage on low land near the sea that keeps flooding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ground' looks like a ship running aground, but it is the signal to rearrange the word next to it.
explanation.definitionFit: A salt marsh is coastal grassland regularly flooded by seawater at high tide.

clue.text: Girl touring major city and port in the Atlantic

indicators.note: touring means going all the way round, so one word surrounds the other

blocks.note: lass is a word for a girl
Palma is the capital of Majorca, so a Majorcan city

explanation.surface: A girl on holiday touring a big city and then an Atlantic port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Major city' looks like 'large city' but hides Majorca, the Spanish island whose capital is Palma.
explanation.definitionFit: Las Palmas is the port city of Gran Canaria in the Canary Islands, out in the Atlantic Ocean.

indicators.note: something injured is damaged out of its proper shape, so the word's letters are reordered

blocks.note: all nine letters are used

explanation.surface: Police dogs have hurt an attacker.
explanation.definitionFit: Alsatian is the usual British name for the German shepherd, a breed of large dog.

indicators.note: in places one word inside the other

blocks.note: a set is a group
Carl is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A wicked boy belonging to a gang.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarlet describes sinfulness, as in a scarlet woman, someone seen as immoral.

indicators.note: surprisingly signals an unexpected outcome, here the letters turning up in an unexpected order

blocks.note: all seven letters of these two words are used

explanation.surface: A poet was the surprising thief.
explanation.definitionFit: T. S. Eliot was the poet of The Waste Land and Four Quartets.

indicators.note: endless means without its end, so the final letter is removed

blocks.note: misery is suffering or hardship

explanation.surface: A stingy person whose meanness brings never-ending hardship to others.
explanation.definitionFit: A miser hoards money and refuses to spend it, the very picture of someone tight-fisted.

blocks.note: mad about something means passionate about it
on means concerning, as in a book on birds
N is the abbreviation for north
A is an abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: A fan who is crazy about a star from North America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passionate about' reads as one phrase, but about is a separate word for concerning.
explanation.definitionFit: Madonna is an American pop star.

clue.text: Race official in agitated state on a road

blocks.note: to be in a stew is to be worked up and anxious
taken as written
Rd is the abbreviation for road

explanation.surface: A race marshal gets flustered standing on a road during the event.
explanation.definitionFit: Stewards are the officials who supervise a horse race or motor race and rule on disputes.

clue.text: Must, round mouth of estuary, come to a stop

indicators.note: a mouth is where something opens, so only the opening letter of the next word is used
round means placed around, so the phrase for must encloses the chosen letter

blocks.note: must means have to
the opening letter of estuary

explanation.surface: A ship must stop near where the river meets the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: HAVE TO goes round E. The nautical surface fits well: heave to is what a ship does to halt at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: To heave to is a sailing term for bringing a vessel to a standstill by setting the sails against each other.

clue.text: Look over lair of a former age

indicators.note: over suggests turning something over, so the word is flipped end to end

blocks.note: lo is an old word meaning look
a den is an animal's lair

explanation.surface: Inspecting the den of some prehistoric creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Look over' reads as one verb meaning inspect, but over tells you to turn the short word for look round.
explanation.definitionFit: Olden is an old-fashioned adjective for long ago, as in the olden days.

blocks.note: a plug is a piece of publicity, an advertisement
dress means clothing in general, as in formal dress

explanation.surface: Someone promotes a clothing brand in the middle of a talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In speech' sounds like a homophone signal, but in is only a link and speech is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An address is a formal talk given to an audience, so it is a speech.

blocks.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
people in league with one another are allied

explanation.surface: A team collecting runs as part of a cricket league.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like an instruction to put one piece inside another, but 'in league' is a single phrase meaning joined together.
explanation.definitionFit: To rally is to recover or improve, as prices or a patient do, which is a sense of picked up.

blocks.note: a chap is a man
a date is a particular point in time

explanation.surface: A man is charged with a crime and is sentenced to time in prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gets time' suggests a prison sentence, but time simply supplies a word for a point on the calendar.
explanation.definitionFit: A mandate is an official instruction or commission, something one is charged with carrying out.

clue.text: Instant deals done in part of New York

indicators.note: done in means destroyed or wrecked, so the letters are broken up and rebuilt

blocks.note: all twelve letters of these two words are used

explanation.surface: Quick business deals being struck in a district of New York City.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Done in' reads as deals completed in a place, but it is the signal that the two words before it are wrecked.
explanation.definitionFit: Staten Island is one of the five boroughs that make up New York City.
